entities.summary:
Hugh of Saint Victor was a Saxon canon regular and a leading theologian and writer on mystical theology, active during the reign of King Stephen of England (1135-1154) and Pope Eugene III (1145-1153).

Born in the 11th century, Hugh's exact birthdate is unknown, but he is believed to have entered the Saint Victor priory in Paris around 1100. He spent most of his life in Paris, where he wrote extensively on mystical theology and became a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of the time.

Hugh's works include the famous 'Didascalicon,' a comprehensive guide to Christian theology, and 'De natura rerum,' a treatise on the nature of things. His writings had a significant impact on the development of scholasticism and the mystical tradition in Western Christianity.

After his death in 1141, Hugh's works were widely disseminated throughout Europe, and his influence can be seen in the writings of later theologians such as Thomas Aquinas.

Hugh's legacy extends beyond the realm of theology, as his writings also contain valuable insights into the intellectual and cultural currents of medieval Europe.

In the 19th century, Hugh's writings were rediscovered by scholars, who recognized the significance of his contributions to the development of Western Christianity.

Today, Hugh of Saint Victor is remembered as one of the most important theologians of the Middle Ages, whose writings continue to be studied and appreciated by scholars around the world.
